title: Accrual Span Used to Settle Promotional Interest on Younger Accounts
content:
The accrual span used to settle promotional interest on an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts is lengthened for accounts still building their balance. Two facts decide it: the count of deposits posted to the account in the three calendar months ending on the correction date, and the whole months the account has been open.

An account open no more than 12 whole months, to which 3 or more deposits posted in that window, takes an accrual span of 62 days.

An account open no more than 12 whole months, to which exactly 2 deposits posted in that window, takes an accrual span of 45 days.

Where fewer than 2 deposits posted in that window, or the account has been open more than 12 whole months, the accrual span is the 31 days of the closed statement month.

### Where the two facts pull apart

The age and the deposit count are conditions on the same span, and both must hold before it is lengthened at all. An account open 30 whole months takes the 31 days of the closed statement month even with 9 deposits in the window, and an account open 3 whole months takes the same 31 days where only 1 deposit posted.

An account open exactly 12 whole months on the correction date still satisfies the age condition, and one open 13 whole months does not. A deposit count of exactly 3 gives 62 days, and a count of exactly 2 gives 45 days.

Take a hypothetical account opened 9 whole months before the correction date with 5 deposits posted in the window: its accrual span is 62 days. Take the same account with 2 deposits in that window: 45 days. Take it opened 30 whole months before the correction date with the same 5 deposits: the 31 days of the closed statement month.
